activities.instructions: Desliza a la derecha si la frase es correcta y a la izquierda si no lo es.
activities.prompt: Mazo de 7 afirmaciones para repasar el tema.

cards.statement: Seeking promotion means hoping to move to a higher position.
cards.explanation: Promotion is advancement within a career.

cards.statement: Income can include money from sources other than a fixed salary.
cards.explanation: Income is a broad term for money received.

cards.statement: A merger is an agreement that joins two companies.
cards.explanation: A merger combines organisations.

cards.statement: Stakeholders can include people outside the company.
cards.explanation: Customers, investors and local residents can be stakeholders.

cards.statement: Revenue is normally calculated only after all costs have been deducted.
cards.explanation: Profit, not revenue, reflects money left after costs.

cards.statement: A business can increase revenue while making less profit.
cards.explanation: Higher costs can reduce profit even when sales rise.

cards.statement: The phrase responsible for introduces an area of duty.
cards.explanation: A manager can be responsible for a budget.

activities.explanation: Cada carta repasa una regla del tema; revisa las falladas al terminar el mazo.

activities.instructions: Desliza a la derecha si la frase es correcta y a la izquierda si no lo es.
activities.prompt: Mazo de 8 afirmaciones para repasar el tema.

cards.statement: Profit is calculated after business costs are taken into account.
cards.explanation: Profit is what remains after costs.

cards.statement: Career and job are interchangeable in every context.
cards.explanation: A job is a particular position; a career is a broader professional path.

cards.statement: Freelance work is always a permanent salaried position.
cards.explanation: Freelancers often work independently on projects.

cards.statement: Stakeholders must be employees of the organisation.
cards.explanation: Stakeholders can be customers, investors or local residents.

cards.statement: To launch a product means to remove it from the market.
cards.explanation: Launch means introduce it to the market.

cards.statement: An applicant is a company that advertises a job.
cards.explanation: An applicant is a person who applies.

cards.statement: The collocation apply for a vacancy is natural in recruitment contexts.
cards.explanation: Applicants apply for jobs and vacancies.

cards.statement: Revenue and profit always mean exactly the same thing.
cards.explanation: Revenue is sales income; profit is revenue after costs.

cards.statement: A workload is the amount of work someone must handle.
cards.explanation: Workload refers to the quantity of work.

cards.statement: A vacancy is an available job position.
cards.explanation: A vacancy is a job that needs to be filled.

cards.statement: To outsource a service is to perform it entirely in-house.
cards.explanation: Outsource means use an external provider.

cards.statement: An employer hires an employee, while an employee works for the employer.
cards.explanation: The terms describe opposite sides of the employment relationship.

cards.statement: A career path describes one isolated shift rather than long-term progression.
cards.explanation: A career path describes professional progression over time.
